question_text: READING(DeviceID, TechID, RecordedAt) and TECHNICIAN(TechID, Name) use ISO date-time strings. Construct SQL listing device IDs read by R. Kim at any time on 12 May 2027.
adaptation_rationale: Rebuilt scenario and response wording while retaining the supported reasoning; source-specific obsolete material excluded.
solution:
One solution:
SELECT r.DeviceID FROM Reading r JOIN Technician t ON r.TechID=t.TechID WHERE t.Name='R. Kim' AND r.RecordedAt >= '2027-05-12 00:00' AND r.RecordedAt < '2027-05-13 00:00';

marking_points.criterion: Includes the whole specified day and excludes other days.

partial_credit_notes: Award independent criteria up to the stated total; accept equivalent technically correct wording/solutions.

verification.technical: SQLite test includes start, last minute and next-day exclusion.
verification.test_code:
import sqlite3
c=sqlite3.connect(':memory:');c.executescript("CREATE TABLE Reading(DeviceID,TechID,RecordedAt);CREATE TABLE Technician(TechID,Name);INSERT INTO Technician VALUES(1,'R. Kim'),(2,'J. Hall');INSERT INTO Reading VALUES('a',1,'2027-05-12 00:00'),('b',1,'2027-05-12 23:59'),('c',1,'2027-05-13 00:00'),('d',2,'2027-05-12 11:00');")
assert c.execute("SELECT r.DeviceID FROM Reading r JOIN Technician t ON r.TechID=t.TechID WHERE t.Name='R. Kim' AND r.RecordedAt >= '2027-05-12 00:00' AND r.RecordedAt < '2027-05-13 00:00'").fetchall()==[('a',),('b',)]
